Only the dual-corded IT load is common to both paths. No electrical tie between the paths elsewhere. Independence of the two utility supplies is NOT claimed.
OHMETRY 2 MW DATA CENTRE: PRELIMINARY SINGLE-LINE DIAGRAM
1. Generated from the master configuration. Every rating shown is a PRELIMINARY ASSUMPTION or UNVERIFIED PLACEHOLDER (see the registers).
2. Fault levels, device ratings, cable sizes, settings and earthing are NOT shown: not calculated or not verified (data pending).
3. Generator basis (ISO 8528 PRP) assumed, not confirmed. Battery not sized. Open transition is a design decision. Closed transition and paralleling with the utility are not shown.
4. Utility A and utility B are drawn as two supplies. Their independence (separate feeders, substations, upstream network) is NOT claimed and is not established.
5. Interlock (concept): ACB-TX and ACB-GEN are shown as interlocked so that the generator bus cannot back-feed the transformer. The interlocking scheme is not designed.
6. Generator paralleling and PMS (concept): each generator has a breaker (GCB) for synchronising. Synchronising, load sharing, load shedding and start/stop logic are functions of a PMS whose
scheme, controller and communications are not designed.
7. UPS (concept): static bypass (STS) and maintenance bypass (MBB) are shown, tapped from the UPS input; whether the bypass has its own feed is a design decision. Battery isolator and DC
8. Protection and metering boundaries: relays, current and voltage transformers, metering, protection zones and settings are not designed and not shown. The utility point of connection and
the UPS vendor scope are boundaries to be agreed.
9. Dual-corded IT load: a single load fed from both IT distribution boards. The path A and path B systems are otherwise separate (no tie shown).
10. Educational and reference use only. Independent review and manufacturer data are needed before any project use.
